feed.title: antxiko — commented disassemblies of 8-bit games
feed.subtitle: Old 8-bit binaries taken apart byte by byte and commented, with the tools to rebuild them: nothing gets claimed that the binary does not show, and the source has to give the original back, byte for byte. Right now that means 100 MSX games.

entry.title: Car Fighter: the sprites, put together from the ROM
entry.summary: A new page: the car in its four directions, the other cars and the truck, hit twice and blowing up, the bomb, the shot and the loose things, and the blast frame by frame, all built from the cartridge's own tables and code. Checked against openMSX: the drawing table identical on 49,805 frames, the cars on 41,057 and the trucks on 1,786.

entry.title: Pachinko U.F.O.: the sprites, put together from the ROM
entry.summary: A new page: the launcher, the windmills, the ball and the U.F.O.s in their steps and colours, and the U.F.O.s frame by frame, all built from the cartridge's own tables. Checked against openMSX: the drawing table identical on 43,152 frames and the whole sprite table on 15,263.

entry.title: Exciting Jockey: the sprites, put together from the ROM
entry.summary: A new page: the horse's ten drawings in the four colours, its four animations (gallop, jump, fall and on the ground) at the pace the code walks them, and the jockey, all built from the cartridge's own tables. Checked against openMSX: the drawing table identical on 44,335 frames and the horses on 62,625.

entry.title: Exciting Baseball: the sprites, put together from the ROM
entry.summary: A new page: every sprite drawing, with the left-hander's flipped on the fly, and the batter through his swing frame by frame, all built from the cartridge's own tables. Checked against openMSX: the drawing table identical on 11,922 frames and the batter on 5,989 with 0 different.

entry.title: Ski Command: the sprites, put together from the ROM
entry.summary: A new page: the skier's eleven drawings, the seven enemies in their four sizes and knocked down, the flying machine in its three colours and hit, and the course objects, all built from the cartridge's own tables; the jump and the crash frame by frame as the code does them. Checked against openMSX: the sprite drawing table identical on 17,989 frames, the skier and the machine with 0 different frames.

entry.title: Five more Casio cartridges, Game Land among them
entry.summary: The Stone of Wisdom, The Seal of Hades, Youkai Yashiki, Issun-boushi no Donnamondai and Game Land, Casio's 1984 kit for making games without programming. Each one 100% explained, reassembled byte for byte and commented to 40% or more; the games played in GIF in openMSX and, in Game Land, a background drawn with its own LINE, BOX, CIRCLE and PAINT and two characters from its samples; the music from each cartridge's own sound engine, checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Fourteen Casio cartridges, taken apart
entry.summary: Fourteen MSX cartridges by Casio, from 1984 to 1986: Ski Command, Exciting Baseball, Exciting Jockey, Pachinko U.F.O., Car Fighter, Ice World, Iga Ninpouchou, Exoide-Z, Shindobaddo Nanatsu no Bouken, Eagle Fighter, Exoide-Z Area 5, Iga Ninpouchou Mangetsu-jou no Tatakai, Koneko no Daibouken and Moai no Hihou. Each one 100% explained, reassembled byte for byte and commented to 40% or more; the titles from running the ROM, checked against openMSX; the games played in GIF in openMSX; the music from each cartridge's own sound engine, checked against openMSX frame by frame.

entry.title: Fred and Ant Attack come to the MSX
entry.summary: Two Quicksilva Spectrum games converted into 64 KB MSX cartridges: native SCREEN 2 rendering, keyboard and PSG layers, disassemblies, reproducible IPS patches and no game image distributed. Araubi completed both games from beginning to end.

entry.title: Konami's Pooyan, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's Pooyan, by Konami and Hudson Soft in 1985 on a Bee Card: its 16 KB 100% explained and commented to 42.7%. The rounds where the wolves come down, the ones where they climb to the rock and the bonus round, the magenta wolf, the ladder, the stone and the boulder played in GIF; the logo and the two screens from the ROM, checked against openMSX; seven tunes from its own engine, identical to openMSX; a loop that never waits for the frame and a script that skips its first step, measured; and the code it shares with the other Konami cartridges in the series.

entry.title: Crazy Train, taken apart
entry.summary: Crazy Train, made by Konami for Sony in 1983: its 8 KB 100% explained and commented to 42.2%. The pushes, the stations, the black trains, the crashes and the cleared stage played in GIF; the first eight boards from the ROM, checked dot by dot against openMSX; the tunes from its own engine; four measured bugs; and the code it shares with the other Konami cartridges in the series.

entry.title: Sparkie: the code it shares with the other Konami cartridges
entry.summary: Sparkie compared instruction by instruction with the other 62 Konami cartridges in the series: none shares a single block with it.

entry.title: Juno First, taken apart
entry.summary: Juno First, made by Konami for Sony in 1983: its 8 KB 100% explained and commented to 41.8%. The waves, the capsule and its astronaut, the WARP, the special wave and the end of the wave played in GIF; the sprites, the ship and the wave picture from the cartridge, checked against openMSX; four tunes from its own engine, whole; and the code it shares with the other Konami cartridges in the series.

entry.title: Sparkie, taken apart
entry.summary: Sparkie, made by Konami for Sony in 1983: its 8 KB 100% explained and commented to 40.7%. The four mazes drawn from the ROM and checked against openMSX byte by byte; the bucket and its wave, the shots, the burning blocks, the bonus, TIME OVER and GAME OVER played in GIF; the characters, the texts and the two tunes from its own sound engine; and a score that breaks past one million points.

entry.title: Quarth, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1990 Quarth for MSX2, its 128 KB 100% explained and commented to 40.3%. The menu, the three modes, the ten stages, the pause and losing, the intro, the three demos and the ending, recorded in openMSX frame by frame and painted in GIF; 19 SCC tunes from its own engine (Metal Gear 2's) checked against openMSX; the texts and the credits, and a rules caption the game never shows.

entry.title: Space Manbow: the three demos, recorded in openMSX
entry.summary: The three recorded demos, whole (stages 1, 2 and 4): since the running cartridge parts from the MSX at frame 68, they are recorded in openMSX, dumping the VRAM, the palette and the registers of every VDP frame, and painted with the same code as the other GIFs. Checked against openMSX screenshots, 0 different pixels; for that the drawing code had two fixes that also redo the other GIFs: register 18 moves the sprites too, and the line interrupts' registers arrive a few lines late.

entry.title: Space Manbow: each enemy on its own, the capsules and a font nobody loads
entry.summary: 79 of the 82 enemy types cut out one by one, painted by the cartridge: each type removed from a copy of the game and what stops being seen. The seven capsule drawings, stage 6's boss fight whole (182 s), the code shared with the other Konami cartridges, a bug hunt (one harmless read of unwritten RAM in the whole game) and an unused font with a loader nothing calls. And the demo: with the Z80 counted in clock cycles it still parts at frame 68, so the pace is not the cause.

entry.title: Space Manbow: where the demo parts from the MSX
entry.summary: Why the recorded demo is not on the page, measured: the RAM at the start of every game frame in openMSX against the running cartridge. Up to frame 67 the game is the same and only what the interrupt moves differs; in frame 68 a shot hits on the MSX and misses here.

entry.title: Space Manbow, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1989 Space Manbow for MSX2, its 256 KB 100% explained and commented to 40.9%. The nine stages drawn whole from the ROM with the cartridge's own map engine and checked tile by tile; the ship and every capsule, the enemies and the nine bosses, the intro and the ending in GIF played by the cartridge at the MSX's pace; the texts translated, 19 SCC tunes from its own engine checked against openMSX, and the debug keys and demo recorder left inside.

entry.title: Metal Gear 2: what it shares with Metal Gear
entry.summary: Both listings compared instruction by instruction: 1,484 bytes of code in runs of 16 bytes or more, 1.3 % of Metal Gear 2 (3.3 % of Metal Gear). What repeats is Konami's MSX2 library: the VDP, 1-3 bit characters turned into 4, the joystick, the Konami logo and the start-up. Sound, bank switching, texts and the guards' intelligence share nothing; the aiming is the same calculation, rewritten. 578 bytes of identical data.

entry.title: Metal Gear 2: all the texts translated, in story order
entry.summary: The transceiver and the texts are now one page: the conversations, the 211 messages of the scenes (Natasha, the sewers, the bridge, Holly, BIG BOSS, the ending, the children) in story order, and the signs, every one next to its translation; the weapon and equipment descriptions too. Also: boss sprite sheets without one-colour flashes, enemy GIFs without a stray Snake, a screen for each part of the intro and the ending, and tunes 0x6B and 0x6E checked along every path a tune is asked for: nothing reaches them.
